preconditions.description: The number of sets n is at least 1 and at most 10,000.
The rank k is at least 1 and at most 100.

postconditions.description: The output consists of n + 1 lines: the first line is the minimum m, and the next n lines are the sets.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= set_element <= m for set in sets for m in range(1, m + 1))
postconditions.description: Each integer in the sets is between 1 and m, inclusive.

postconditions.expression: all(all(gcd(s_i, s_j) == k for i < j for s_i, s_j in combinations(set, 2)) for set in sets)
postconditions.description: Each set has the rank k, meaning that the gcd of every pair of distinct elements in the set is k.

postconditions.expression: all_unique(set_element for set in sets for set_element in set)
postconditions.description: Each integer is used at most once across all sets.
The value of m is the smallest possible value that allows the construction of n sets of rank k with no integer used more than once.

invariants.description: The minimum value of m must be at least 4 to form sets of 4 distinct integers.
